FOLDED CLAUSE (step-3b conditional-mean production law; formerly H3B-step3b-mean): For each fixed epoch table T, with a fresh class-kept chaining value CV drawn under H1, let G_T(CV) be the number of step3b calls and S_T(CV) their total counted stopped-path work. H3B asserts E[S_T(CV) | T] <= 842.361097 E[G_T(CV) | T]. The charged source implements early stopping before later trace rows are constructed.

FOLDED CLAUSE (within-CV dependence and factorial-moment production law; formerly H3-P1-within-cv-dependence): Group independence within a chaining value (the form of H5-group-independence of the accepted 44870635): good pairs of one chaining value that share no endpoint (a0 or u) are independent trials of the accepted event, each with probability q3r; good pairs sharing an endpoint form a group counted once. Consequence used: for a uniform chaining value and any table, J (accepted good pairs among all claws of the chaining value) has E[J(J-1)] <= 2^-7.5 E[J]. This filing applies the same premise to the kept-CV class ((cv0 >> 24) & 62 == 12): the class conditions only cv[0], the panel below is drawn from uniform chaining values (so about 1/32 of its CVs are in-class), and the transfer of the second-moment bound to the class-conditioned law is part of this declared premise.

heuristics.statement:
The sequential Monte Carlo estimator traillab (the lineage's own C tool, not shipped), with which q3_model and the paired difference D_LB were measured, estimates the accepted-event rate of the stated model without material bias. It replays every sample on real 38-step compressions of both members (0 replay mismatches required), treats rows 16..21 as the importance-split prefix (8,192 particles, 256 proposals per row; the row-16 stage is exact with weight 160/2^32) and counts EXACT (zero output difference after step 37) in the window rows 22..37. Its per-seed values, combined by the registered one-sided rules, give conservative bounds for the true rate.

Under Section 7's deterministic full-cycle ustart product bound, no per-table Lemma T or a-bar upper bound is required.
